answer: An agent market can tie full reward rights to proven breadth across many unrelated task domains: translation, code review, shipping logs at a busy wharf, each checked by different verifiers. A real agent adapts and builds a broad record; a sybil farm cloned from one cheap copper-wire pipeline aces only its niche, so each clone stays capped in a low tier. Cracking that hard walnut means paying for real skill per clone, which kills the farm's margin.
